content: Readwise Daily Review resurfaces highlights via a decaying recall-probability model rather than fixed dates: unprocessed or new highlights are shown stochastically in the first half of the review; Mastery cards use spaced repetition with configurable initial half-lives such as seven, fourteen, or twenty-eight days, and resurface once recall probability drops to about fifty percent. Users can up or down weight specific sources and bias toward newer or older content. Key UX lesson: resurfacing feels good when it is low-volume and digest-sized rather than a flood, decays based on the user's own engagement signal such as dismiss or like, and lets users tune source weighting rather than imposing a rigid algorithm.
